title: The expedited partner therapy prescription under 105 CMR 721.000: the electronic prescribing exception in 721.070(A)(7), no pharmacist verification under 721.070(C), and the blank name and address under 721.020(D)(4)
subtopic: Electronic prescribing exception, pharmacist verification and the patient name and address for expedited partner therapy prescriptions
rule_summary: 105 CMR 721.070(A) provides that the Prescriptions it lists shall not be required to be issued as Electronic Prescriptions, and may be issued as Written or Oral Prescriptions, provided, however, that Oral Prescriptions must comply with 105 CMR 721.070(B) and that no Written or Oral Prescription may be issued under any exception enumerated in 105 CMR 721.070(A) in an effort to circumvent the requirement to issue an Electronic Prescription. Paragraph (7) lists Prescriptions issued pursuant to 105 CMR 700.003(J) for expedited partner therapy for treatment of chlamydia, which are intended for dispensing to the patient's partner. Under 105 CMR 721.070(C), a pharmacist who receives an otherwise valid Written or Oral Prescription is not required to verify that such Prescription properly falls under one of the exceptions from the requirement to electronically prescribe, including a waiver under 105 CMR 721.070(A)(3). Under 105 CMR 721.020(D)(4), the Prescription shall contain the name and address of the patient, except in a veterinary Prescription, a Prescription for naloxone or other opioid antagonist approved by the Department, or a Prescription issued pursuant to 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7) or 105 CMR 721.070(A)(12), in which case the name and address may be left blank; provided however, the person taking delivery of the Prescription for naloxone or other opioid antagonist as approved by the Department may, but is not required to, be used in place of the name of the patient.
exam_relevance: Tests how the prescription format regulation treats an expedited partner therapy prescription: it need not be electronic, the patient's name and address may be left blank, and a pharmacist who receives an otherwise valid written or oral prescription need not verify that it falls under an exception.

authority.name: Electronic prescribing exceptions, including expedited partner therapy prescriptions, and pharmacist verification of an exception
Name and address of the patient on the prescription and when it may be left blank

common_confusions: Reading 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7) as reaching partner prescriptions for any sexually transmitted infection; it describes prescriptions for expedited partner therapy for treatment of chlamydia intended for dispensing to the patient's partner.

Expecting the paragraph that 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7) cites to be the expedited partner therapy provision; 721.070(A)(7) cites 105 CMR 700.003(J), while the current publication of 105 CMR 700.000 provides for expedited partner therapy in 105 CMR 700.003(H) and its 700.003(J) concerns medical device manufacturers.

Assuming a pharmacist must confirm that an otherwise valid written or oral prescription properly falls under an exception from electronic prescribing; 105 CMR 721.070(C) says the pharmacist is not required to verify that.

Treating a blank patient name and address as permitted only on a veterinary prescription; 105 CMR 721.020(D)(4) also names naloxone or other Department-approved opioid antagonist prescriptions and prescriptions issued under 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7) or (A)(12).
verification_notes: Read 105 CMR 721.070(A), including paragraphs (7) and (12), 105 CMR 721.070(C) and 105 CMR 721.020(D)(4) in the current 105 CMR 721.000 publication on mass.gov (pages dated 9/27/24) on 2026-09-16, and compared the cross-reference in 105 CMR 721.070(A)(7) with 105 CMR 700.003(H) and (J) in the current 105 CMR 700.000 publication on mass.gov read the same day.
